question: Which of the following correctly describes how potential difference between two points is calculated?

options.text: Potential difference = Work done × Potential energy

solution:
The correct answer is __**Potential difference = Work done ÷ Charge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Definition of Potential Difference:** The potential difference between two points is defined as the amount of **work done** to move a unit charge from one point to another. It is mathematically represented as **Potential Difference = Work done ÷ Charge**, which is the correct formula.
 
• **SI Unit:** The SI unit of potential difference is the **Volt (V)**. One volt is defined as one joule of work done per coulomb of charge.
 
• **Application of Formula:** This formula is fundamental in understanding various concepts of electricity, including **Ohm’s Law, electric circuits, and energy transfer** in electrical systems.
 
• **Physical Meaning:** The potential difference gives a measure of the energy required to move electric charges between two points. It is equivalent to the amount of **energy provided or consumed** in the system.
 
• **Correctness of Statement:** Option 1 correctly describes how potential difference is calculated, as it aligns with the standard definition and usage in physics. *Hence, the correct answer is Option 1.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Formulas Related to Electricity:**

 
 
• **Ohm’s Law:** Voltage (V) = Current (I) × Resistance (R). This fundamental law connects potential difference, current, and resistance in electrical circuits.
 
• **Power Formula:** Power (P) = Voltage (V) × Current (I). This helps calculate the rate of energy transfer in electrical systems.
 
• **Energy Formula:** Energy (E) = Voltage (V) × Charge (Q). This represents the total energy used or produced by an electrical system.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Electric Potential:**
 
 
• Electric potential is a **scalar quantity**.
 
• The direction of movement of charge depends on whether the potential difference is positive or negative.
 
• It is measured using devices like a **voltmeter**.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Potential Difference:**
 
 
• It is essential for powering devices and machines, enabling them to perform work.
 
• Potential difference is used in **batteries, capacitors, and generators** to store and transfer energy.
 
• It is crucial in designing electrical systems for industries, homes, and transportation.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• In a **circuit with a battery**, the battery provides a potential difference to allow current to flow.
 
• A bulb lights up because of the potential difference across its terminals, enabling energy transfer.
 
• In a **capacitor**, the potential difference is used to store electrical energy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option Analysis:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** Correct formula for potential difference as per the definition. *Correct.*
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect, as charge should not be divided by work done.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect, potential difference is not calculated using work done multiplied by potential energy.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect, charge multiplied by work done does not represent potential difference.
 
 
 
• **Relation to Energy Transfer:** The concept of potential difference is central to understanding how **electrical energy is converted into other forms of energy**, such as light and heat.
 
• **Devices for Measurement:** Potential difference is measured using a **voltmeter**, which is connected in parallel to the component being measured.
 
• **Historical Insight:** The term “volt” was named after **Alessandro Volta**, an Italian scientist who invented the electric battery.
